sampling_model.design: Population identification uses a square fully observed cyclic LiNG model with independent nondegenerate errors and at most one Gaussian coordinate. Inference uses independent observations from one fixed law in the FOBI subclass, whose eigengaps are gaps among distinct centered standardized fourth cumulants.
sampling_model.units: The observations \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\) are independent draws from one fixed \(q\)-variate equilibrium law.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no treatment variable in the core identification theorem; a later atomic intervention reveals a matching edge and is the downstream consumer.
sampling_model.overlap: No propensity-score overlap condition is used.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The sample covariance whitens the observations, the sample FOBI eigensystem estimates row directions, and the plug-in influence functions calibrate a symmetrized matrix region. Because empirical eigenvector signs may change, covariance consistency is asserted only modulo signed-row conjugacy. Coverage and contraction are pointwise; no graph support is assumed known, and no uniform claim is made near vanishing FOBI eigengaps, zero normalization denominators, or unit-circle stability boundaries.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: LiNG-D outputs the complete distribution-entailment equivalence class and stability selects at most one candidate when the true graph has disjoint cycles.
Distribution-equivalent cyclic LiNG graphs correspond to perfect matchings, their SCCs are invariant, and unfiltered matching samples estimate intervention reward.
The permanent of every nonnegative matrix has a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme.
Counting independent sets is \(\#\mathrm P\)-complete even for graphs of maximum degree three.
At activity one, independent-set counting has a deterministic FPTAS on graphs of maximum degree five.
Unless \(\mathrm{NP}=\mathrm{RP}\), no FPRAS counts independent sets on graphs of maximum degree six.
All perfect matchings of a bipartite graph can be enumerated in output-sensitive total time with linear work per matching after preprocessing.
Under bounded eighth moments and distinct kurtoses, the FOBI unmixing estimator has an explicit joint root-sample-size expansion.
Inversion of a sample criterion yields confidence regions for an identified parameter set with consistency and coverage theory.
Discontinuity of a functional prevents nontrivial locally uniform confidence procedures in general.
StableSpIn learns cyclic linear models under the absolute spectral-radius restriction \(\rho(|B|)<1\).

body.tldr: A fully observed cyclic LiNG law identifies a finite monomial row-assignment orbit, while equilibrium stability imposes a global spectral filter on that orbit. The explicit rational \(3n\)-variable construction \(W_G\) has complete stable orbit \(\{\pi_S:S\in\mathcal I(G)\}\), with graph-uniform radial margins established by a pole-free, multiplicity-preserving analytic determinant homotopy. On fixed-labelled gadget images, exact counting is in \(\mathrm{FP}\) through degree two and \(\#\mathrm P\)-complete already at degree three; approximation has a deterministic FPTAS through degree five and no FPRAS at degree six unless \(\mathrm{RP}=\mathrm{NP}\). Hardness also persists on coned gadget images whose coefficient-support digraph is one SCC, without a bounded-degree promise, so it is not caused by multiplying SCC-local counts. In contrast, the unfiltered orbit is a permanent with an FPRAS. Admissible and stable orbit counts factor exactly over SCCs for every real equation matrix; only the enumerator and its Lyapunov and bit-complexity guarantees are restricted to rational stable-reference inputs. Symmetrized FOBI-region inversion gives pointwise signed-orbit-honest count coverage, without a uniform graph-support or stability-boundary claim.

project_justification.gap: Published cyclic-LiNG methods describe the normalized row-assignment fiber and may screen individual candidates by stability, but they do not classify the stability-filtered count, locate its bounded-degree exact and approximation thresholds, or show whether hardness survives inside one feedback SCC. Donor results for independent sets and permanent-based sampling do not themselves provide a coefficient-valid cyclic-LiNG transfer.
project_justification.niche: The missing bridge is a rational coefficient construction that controls normalization, all unintended permutations, analytic multiplicity, Schur-complement poles, polynomial-bit spectral margins, and the support-SCC geometry uniformly over the donor graph.
project_justification.fill: The graph gadget identifies its complete stable orbit with independent sets. On fixed-labelled gadget images this yields the exact degree-two/three and approximation degree-five/six elbows, while a cone reduction proves exact and approximate hardness on one-SCC images. The note separately proves admissible and stable SCC factorization for arbitrary real equation matrices, an output-sensitive local enumerator on rational stable-reference inputs, and pointwise symmetrized FOBI confidence-image coverage modulo the signed row orbit.

body.related_work: Lacerda, Spirtes, Ramsey, and Hoyer characterize the cyclic LiNG row-permutation fiber and use Schur stability to screen candidates, but do not realize arbitrary independent-set systems or classify the filtered count. Sharifian, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash represent the ambiguity by perfect matchings, establish SCC invariance, and use unfiltered matching samples for intervention rewards; their sampler does not impose equilibrium stability, and must be conditioned on the stable orbit when stability is additionally required. Valiant supplies the general exact-counting donor, Greenhill proves exact independent-set hardness at degree three, Weitz gives the deterministic hard-core approximation scheme applicable at activity one through degree five, and Sly supplies the degree-six inapproximability donor. Those are graph results: the coefficient-valid, count-preserving transfer and the exclusion of unintended normalized assignments come from the present realization theorem. Jerrum, Sinclair, and Vigoda provide the nonnegative-permanent FPRAS for the unfiltered benchmark. The FOBI limit uses distinct centered standardized fourth cumulants and is symmetrized over signed row assignments, so covariance convergence is required only modulo signed-row conjugacy.
body.interpretation: The causal target is the number of Schur-stable mechanisms in the population-identified normalized ICA row orbit, not an arbitrary count attached to one ICA labeling and not an effect estimand. On the gadget image, equality with \(|\mathcal I(G)|\) is proved rather than stipulated. The fixed-labelled images exhibit exact degree-two/three and approximation degree-five/six thresholds, and the cone construction shows that hardness remains when the coefficient-support digraph itself has one SCC. Exact SCC factorization for arbitrary real equation matrices therefore isolates components algebraically but does not make the within-component stability filter easy. The matching-frequency sampler and adaptive intervention rule of Sharifian, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash use the unfiltered matching orbit; when equilibrium stability is additionally imposed, their frequencies and rewards must instead be conditioned on the stable orbit. The permanent FPRAS for all admissible assignments does not approximate those conditioned frequencies by itself.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The degree-two/three exact and degree-five/six approximation phase diagram is proved only on fixed-labelled gadget images, where the donor graph is recoverable in polynomial time. The one-SCC cone reduction deliberately carries no bounded-degree promise because its universal vertex has unbounded degree. Admissible and stable SCC factorization is algebraic and holds for every real equation matrix, but the local enumerator, exact Lyapunov screening, and stated bit-complexity bounds apply only to the rational stable-reference class \(\mathcal R_q\) and are output-sensitive in local admissible matchings rather than stable outputs alone. The analytic proof uses conservative contour constants; the complete-orbit computations for \(K_2\), \(P_5\), \(C_5\), \(K_{1,4}\), and \(K_5\) are finite sanity checks, not substitutes for the uniform proof. FOBI covariance convergence is only modulo signed-row conjugacy, and confidence-image coverage is pointwise, not uniform near graph-support, eigengap, normalization, or unit-circle boundaries.
body.honest_scope: The phase diagram concerns the promised fixed-labelled gadget images, not all sparse cyclic LiNG matrices. The one-SCC result establishes hardness persistence but makes no bounded-degree claim. Admissible and Schur-stable orbit factorization holds for arbitrary real equation matrices without rationality, invertibility, unit diagonal, or stable-reference assumptions. Enumeration, exact Lyapunov certification, and their bit bounds are asserted only on \(\mathcal R_q\), with work depending on enumerated local admissible matchings. The note does not provide an almost-uniform generator for the stable orbit, stability-conditioned adaptive submodularity, or a uniform graph-support recovery theorem. The FOBI result assumes distinct centered standardized fourth cumulants and gives pointwise signed-orbit-honest confidence-image coverage; it makes no uniform singleton-count claim at discontinuity boundaries.
